Man Charged With Attempted Murder In Shooting Of SWAT Officer, Woman In Albany Park

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:53
Instaread
Daniel Aguirre, 42, was arrested after he shot a 67-year-old woman and the officer and held a 14-year-old girl and another woman at gunpoint inside a home, police said.
by Alex V. Hernandez July 22, 2026July 23, 2026

CHICAGO — An Albany Park man accused of shooting a Chicago police SWAT officer and the mother of his longtime partner had become “increasingly paranoid” before he held his partner and their daughter hostage Monday at their North Side home, prosecutors said Wednesday.

Daniel Aguirre, of the 4600 block of North Springfield Avenue, was charged Wednesday with six felonies, including attempted murder, aggravated unlawful restraint, aggravated assault of a peace officer and aggravated discharge of a firearm at an occupied building, officials said.

Officials said he admitted to shooting at the door during the standoff, striking his partner’s mother as she stood outside of the apartment where the situation unfolded, and later at police as they tried to get inside.

Aguirre, 42, was ordered detained during a Wednesday hearing at the George N. Leighton Criminal Courthouse, 2650 S. California Ave.

“This case is in the earliest stage of what will likely be a complex and lengthy legal process,” a spokesperson for the Cook County Public Defender’s Office, which is representing Aguirre, said via email: “We would remind the public that statements made by police and prosecutors are only allegations and that cases can change significantly from this initial stage as they are investigated further.”

In a proffer detailing Monday’s incident released Wednesday, prosecutors identified the two people Aguirre held hostage as his 42-year-old “longtime partner” and their 14-year-old daughter, who police initially said was 13. The woman who was shot was identified as the 67-year-old mother of Aguirre’s mother.

That woman and the SWAT officer are currently listed in stable condition, the proffer said.

The family lives together at an apartment building in the 4600 block of North Springfield Avenue, with Aguirre and his partner living in the second floor unit with their daughter, the proffer said.

Starting in May, Aguirre became “increasingly paranoid” his partner was cheating on him and having him followed, prosecutors said. Sunday, the couple got into an argument about “his paranoia” and Aguirre headbutted her, the proffer said.

When his partner woke up Monday morning, Aguirre continued making accusations, including that she had poisoned him, which led to another confrontation where Aguirre “pushed her down on a couch and pointed a gun at her head,” the proffer said. He also punched his daughter and later “tried stomping on her head,” the proffer states.

He later held the two at gunpoint in the apartment’s living room, the proffer said.

The 67-year-old woman, who lives in the first floor apartment, went to investigate the commotion on the second floor apartment along with another relative, the proffer said.

As the women knocked on the door of the second floor and asked Aguirre to let them in, he fired his gun through the door — hitting his partner’s mother in the face, the proffer said. She was later taken to Illinois Masonic Medical Center in critical condition.

Aguirre fired at the door again and then “turned the burners of the stove on and began pacing throughout the apartment,” prosecutors said. Aguirre’s partner was able to discreetly call 911 while pleading with him to turn off the stove, the proffer said.

Aguirre complied but also used the butt of a kitchen knife to strike his partner before noting he had eight bullets left, prosecutors said. “One for me, two for you. That means I can kill five of them,” he allegedly said.

When the SWAT team came inside the building and tried to enter the home using a battering ram, Aguirre shot through the door again and struck an officer, authorities said. A .38 caliber semiautomatic handgun and 18 spent shell casings were recovered at the scene, officials said.

Police then were able to negotiate with Aguirre over his partner’s phone, and he eventually released the hostages before turning himself in. The girl had “visible bruising and scratches” while her mother had “two visible black eyes,” the proffer said. They were both taken to Stroger Hospital.

Aguirre had previously domestic battery arrests in 2004 and 2008 that were subsequently dismissed, according to prosecutors. 

His next court date is Aug. 12.
